text:
maya: Dropping an nsys trace + perfetto heatmap for the KV-write hotspot seen on fusion variants. saw a p95 token latency spike on a few dedicated nodes this morning, traced to a write-heavy microworkload. attaching notes.

luca: Thanks — quick q: which model/config and seq len? cold start or steady state?

maya: model=llama-2-13b q4_K_M, seq=2048, batch size varied 1..8. workload is a streaming chat style with a lot of KV writes (we keep flushing small prefixes). steady-state after ~30s. routing picked flash-attn-v3-fused for most shards.

arjun: Can you paste the top kernels from nsys (by gpu_time)? curious if it's compute or mem-bound.

maya: top kernels (nsys summary):
```
1) flash_attn_fused_forward  36.2ms  (46%)
2) kv_write_kernel         15.8ms  (20%)
3) flash_attn_copy_kv      9.1ms   (12%)
4) softmax_stable          4.5ms   (6%)
5) atomic_idx_inc          3.9ms   (5%)
```
note: nvprof shows kv_write_kernel has a high number of divergent branches and low achieved occupancy. perfetto shows repeated small writes interleaved with flash kernels leading to SM contention.

luca: Interesting. So the fused flash kernel dominates but kv_write is the tail contributor. Could be serialization when multiple warps update the same KV banks. did you capture bank heatmap?

maya: yes — perfetto heatmap attached (slice): when prefix length ~128 we get concentrated writes to low-index banks. bank stride ~32 -> collisions. heatmap shows spikes aligned with flash_attn_fused_forward ranges.

perf-bot: nvprof excerpt: "GPU activities: kernel: kv_write_kernel 42.1% stalls on memory dependency; achieved occupancy 24%"

arjun: Two hypotheses: 1) fused variant intermixes KV writes and compute in a way that amplifies bank conflicts; 2) our kvcache write path uses atomics that cause serialization when writes hit same cacheline.

jen: Do we have a baseline (non-fused flash or split-attn) for the same traffic pattern? need to know if this is a regression or expected tradeoff.

maya: baseline (non-fused pipeline) numbers:
- p50 latency tokens/sec: 980
- p95 latency tokens/sec: 720
- kv_write_kernel time: 8.6ms

current (fused) numbers:
- p50: 940 ( -4% )
- p95: 520 ( -28% )
- kv_write_kernel: 15.8ms ( +84% )
commit window points at commit abc123 (runtime:kernel-selection) deployed ~03:12 UTC.

luca: that's a pretty big tail regression. suggests kernel selection heuristic started preferring fused variant in cases with high write_ratio. we should tweak selection: if write_ratio > 0.3 prefer non-fused variant.

arjun: Also try a quick experiment: disable KV in-register buffering for fused variant so writes are batched to shared mem then flushed as a single coalesced store. Might reduce atomic pressure.

maya: ran an A/B with heuristic override on a small fleet: forcing non-fused reduced kv_write_kernel to 7.9ms and p95 recovered to ~700. Perf numbers reproducible across 3 nodes.

jen: Good. What's next? rollback to baseline or change heuristic? need risk assessment.

maya: plan: 1) temporary heuristic change: prefer non-fused when write_ratio>0.25 (hotfix) 2) follow-up: micro-optimizations on kv_write_kernel (coalescing + bank-aware allocator) 3) longer-term: add a runtime sampler that flags high bank-collision patterns to auto-switch kernels.

infra-bot: deploy:hotfix started by maya at 1946234585 on prod-dedicated-us-west-2 (rollout 10%). link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/roll/9876

perf-bot: sliced nsys id=trace-1946234567 link: https://perf.redwood/trace/1946234567 (contains perfetto heatmap + kernel timeline)

luca: quick note — arjun, when you work the coalescing patch, add a unit test that simulates skewed bank strides (stride % banks == 0) so we don't regress again.

arjun: Will do. also going to instrument NVTX ranges around kvcache alloc/free to correlate with perfetto heat slices.

maya: one more datapoint: memory bandwidth didn't saturate; it's more about serialization and warp divergence. profiler shows high non-coherent atomic retries.

jen: Thanks all. Can someone put a short postmortem in incidents/ if the hotfix goes to 100%? capture root cause, mitigation, and next steps.

maya: will draft a short incident note after rollout completes.

luca: love the quick triage. keeping kernel selection heuristics conservative for write-heavy workloads seems low-risk.

maya: update: hotfix reached 100% at 1946234612; rolling metrics look good — tail latency trending back to baseline. will follow up with micro-optimizations ticket.

arjun: created follow-up ticket #INF-3145: "kvcache: bank-aware coalesced writes + fused variant guardrails"

jen: ack. thanks team. :thumbsup:
